root_causes: The original renderer requires UUID, username and color data supplied by AssetsWebSocket cosmetics packets; enabling the setting alone cannot create that data, including for the local player.
The sneaking nametag path renders text directly and never draws the logo.

The dedicated icon helper forced depthMask(false), including the visible and sneaking label passes where text writes depth. Later translucent blocks and entities could therefore cover icon pixels while the text remained protected.
That helper disabled blending with raw GL calls, leaving GlStateManager's cached blend state inconsistent for subsequent nametag draws. Raw logo color calls also bypassed its color cache.
The 88x100 logo texture used nearest-neighbor sampling on a 13x7 world-space quad, causing abrupt texel changes during subpixel camera movement.
changes: Use a local logo identity fallback for the current player when service data is absent, without inserting a fabricated entry into the shared identity map.
Keep remote logos restricted to recognized player UUIDs and preserve subicons. Both local and remote logos use the shared red-C, white-B texture instead of service-supplied tint colors.
Match the entity username after removing formatting codes; allow the local Nick Hider alias, and exclude partial usernames and unrelated score labels.
Share the text and logo drawing routine with sneaking nametags and reserve space for the logo in both paths.
Size the normal nametag background using the displayed name, including Nick Hider substitution.
Nametag and Tablist both reference PlayerNametagStyle.LOGO_TEXTURE (client/logo_white.png); normal and sneaking nametags retain their opacity, shadow and subicon settings.

Use the dedicated Tessellator renderer for logos, shadows and subicons, inheriting the label pass depth mask, depth test and blending. The visible and sneaking passes write depth like text; the through-wall pass continues without depth writes. All vertices retain their existing z=0 coordinates and GL_LEQUAL permits coplanar shadow/foreground overlap.
Use GlStateManager for nametag icon colors and temporarily enable linear texture filtering, restoring the previous texture filters after drawing.
usage: Enable Nametag and Show CheatBreaker Logo. To view your own label, also enable Shown own Nametag and use third-person view. Remote player recognition still requires service data.

validation.full_build: mvnw.cmd clean package: BUILD SUCCESS; exit code 0

coverage: Actual CB texture and production RenderUtil.drawNametagIcon in a 128x128 LWJGL Pbuffer with a 24-bit depth buffer.
Later opaque entity-like and translucent block-like geometry behind the icon cannot overwrite its visible pixels at rotations 0, 23 and -41 degrees and fractional positions.
Coplanar shadow and foreground render with GL_LEQUAL; icon alpha holes leave later geometry visible.
Modelview matrix, texture filtering, depth write mask, depth test and blend enable state remain unchanged by the helper.
Through-wall alpha=32/255 pass retains disabled depth test/writes and leaves the depth buffer untouched; no OpenGL errors.
opengl_probe.negative_control: The same probe against the previous HEAD RenderUtil fails with No icon depth coverage, confirming that it detects the original defect.

performance.removed: One depth-mask state read and two GlStateManager.depthMask calls per icon/shadow/subicon draw.
performance.unchanged: Existing quad geometry, texture filtering and caller render passes.
performance.depth_behavior: Visible icon fragments now write depth as text already does; alpha-tested transparent pixels do not write depth.
